title: Quentin Grimes scores 42 points to spark Lakers comeback vs. Hornets

 Andrés Soto USA TODAY Updated Nov. 18, 2026, 2:06 a.m. ET Hear this story It's the Quentin Grimes game.
 Things were looking bleak for the Los Angeles Lakers , who entered the fourth quarter on Tuesday night trailing the Charlotte Hornets by 13. But with Luka Dončić on the bench to begin the final frame, it was Grimes who took over to bring the Lakers back. Grimes scored a career-high 47 points in the 118-114 overtime win. He was 10 of 14 from long range, a new career-high in 3s made.
 Dončić checked back in midway through the quarter and has quickly benefitted from Charlotte now having to focus on Grimes defensively; he drained a game-tying three with three minutes to go, though the Hornets ultimately regained the lead.
 With eight seconds left in regulation, Matisse Thybulle grabbed a missed Coby White free throw and fed it to Dončić, who made his way to the 3-point line but ultimately found Grimes on the opposite wing.
 Dončić gave the Lakers the lead in OT – their first since the second quarter – on a fadeaway at the 3:15 mark.
